text: The two story files 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P4 rwb-access (Access and authority)/RWB P4 AD005 APP Separation of duty check at sign-in v1.md and RWB P4 AD005 CON Separation of duty check at sign-in - contract v1.md, and the fragments _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P4-AD005-APP.json and RWB-P4-AD005-CON.json, all already present in the tree and written by the parallel Work Package B-P4-02 for the same two slices of legacy RWB-AD-005, stand as the deliverable of B2-P4-004: they are not rewritten, not versioned to v2, not duplicated, and their missing values stay registered once as CG-B-P4-02-AD005-1 and CG-B-P4-02-AD005-2 with ASM-B-P4-02-AD005-1 to ASM-B-P4-02-AD005-13. Their metadata rows, their 19 sections, AC1 and AC2 of RWB-AD-005 with the origin tags on the APP file, the eight (new, D-RCV-60) criteria of the CON file, the shared pair RW-WRITEOFF and RW-WOCOMM, the four legacy test case IDs TC-AD-005-01 to TC-AD-005-04 with the Level column, the nine section 12 tables and the citation set are kept unchanged, and B2-P4-004 registers only the duplicate-Work-Package finding.
why: The Work Package names the two story files and the two fragments as its outputs and every one of them already exists with complete content, because the plan issues two Work Packages for one legacy key (B-P4-02 with fanout 5 and B2-P4-004 with fanout 0). Root AGENTS.md rule 1 forbids editing a file that already exists and forbids writing a path outside the 'Write only' block, so the next-version copy that rule 1 would otherwise ask for cannot be created here (a v2 file is not a listed output), and rule 13 forbids stopping the run. The existing artefacts were therefore read, verified against Template and Rules v1 R7, R7.1, R7.2, R8.1 and R9 with the P4 context pack as the authority for service facts, and kept; the collision is recorded as one gap row and this row, in the same way as the parallel B2-P4-002 finding for RWB-AD-003.
read: _work/msr/wp/B-P4-02.md and _work/msr/wp/B2-P4-004.md (the same four output paths, fanout 5 and fanout 0); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (slices RWB-P4-AD005-CON in CG-W4 and RWB-P4-AD005-APP in L-P4-A, legacy RWB-AD-005 disposition Split (rework), wave 4); _work/msr/context/P4.md (service row, ownership rows, naming rules, slides 4, 5, 8, 10 and 13); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md heading RWB-AD-005 (story statement, AC1 and AC2, Data, Endpoints, screens, permission checks, messages, test cases, guardrails); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md and _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md through the two story files; the two delivered story files and the two fragments; _work/msr/gaps/B-P4-02-AD005.part.jsonl (2 rows) and _work/msr/assumptions/B-P4-02-AD005.part.jsonl (13 rows); _work/msr/status.json
applied_in: B2-P4-004: the four artefacts left unchanged, no value re-registered and no row duplicated; _work/msr/gaps/B2-P4-004.jsonl (1 row); _work/msr/assumptions/B2-P4-004.jsonl (1 row); _work/msr/editlog/B2-P4-004.md
confirm: Delivery lead and the stage B2 coordinator at the wave 4 batch close, when the plan is de-duplicated and the B-P4-02 title is closed with its edit log row
impact: If the coordinator instead wants B2-P4-004 to own the two files, they must be rewritten from legacy RWB-AD-005 with a new set of CG and ASM citations of the form CG-B2-P4-004-n, which invalidates the 15 identifiers the delivered artefacts cite and the cross-references the sibling files RWB P4 AD001, AD002, AD003, AD004, AD006, E1022 and E1037 make to this key; the rewrite changes no business content, because the two files already answer AC1 and AC2 word for word and carry all nine contract tables
